svg.text: Motion alarm with a PIR, a TM1637 count and a buzzer
LP-MSPM0G3519, seen from above, USB unplugged. Add the wires in the numbered order; each number sits at both ends of its wire and in the list below. The schematic shows the same circuit in symbols.
J1 and J2 are the outer columns, J3 and J4 the inner ones; pin 1, 21, 40 and 20 are at the USB end.
Wire colours: red 3.3 V, orange 5 V, black ground; every other colour is one signal.

g.text: Breadboard: holes a to e, and f to j, in one column are joined; each long rail is joined end to end.
Column 1 is at this end; rails and holes count up toward the top.
Wires, in the order you add them
Ground rail (blue, hole 2) to J2 pin 20 (GND)
Place first: 330 ohm resistor, Passive buzzer
Buzzer resistor, breadboard j14 to J2 pin 14 (PB7)
Buzzer minus, breadboard j20 to Ground rail
PIR VCC (5 V) to J3 pin 21 (5V)
330 ohm resistor: one leg in h14, other leg in h17
Passive buzzer: + leg in f17, − leg in f20
PIR motion sensor: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
TM1637 4-digit display: beside the breadboard, pins toward the wires
The buzzer draws about 10 mA through its 330 ohm resistor, within what one pin may give.
The PIR runs on 5 V; its OUT pin swings only to 3.3 V, so it is safe into the LaunchPad. Pin order varies by maker: read the silkscreen under the dome.
The TM1637 module's pins read CLK DIO VCC GND on most boards; check yours.
Then plug in USB, run the build, and expect
The display counts motion events: 0001, 0002, and so on.
The same circuit as a schematic

svg.text: Fox Red Labs. Pins from the build's pin table, the one the program is built from; the 3D build on the page shows the same wiring step by step. Board picture: TI SLAU947 cover render.
